race.name: Ukiah Mendo Gravel Epic
race.tagline: A redwood-heavy series finale with 8,420 feet, private roads, and no free coast to the line.

vitals.field_size: Several hundred riders; exact 2026 count not published
vitals.registration: 2027 registration is open through the organizer's Movemint link; the event page still carries earlier-edition deadline details
vitals.prize_purse: Cash prizes for top three pro men and women in 2026
vitals.aid_stations: Miles 15.8, 32, and 57 for the 2026 long course

logistics.explanation: Ukiah has usable lodging and a compact event base, but separate staging plus access restrictions on private Mendocino Redwood Company roads require attention.

length.explanation: Seventy-six miles is a substantial race day without crossing into ultra-distance territory.

technicality.explanation: The organizer recommends 40-42 mm treaded tires, and 2026 coverage documented punctures and a decisive final dirt descent, but this remains gravel rather than singletrack racing.

elevation.explanation: The course gains 8,420 feet, starting with roughly 1,900 feet in eight miles and reserving another major climb for the final third.

climate.explanation: Late May usually brings cool mornings and mild-to-warm afternoons, with wind on exposed ridges more likely to matter than extreme temperature.

altitude.explanation: The Mendocino hills are demanding but low enough that altitude is not a primary physiological stress.

adventure.explanation: One-day access through private redwood property and the long transition between Ukiah and the coast make the route feel larger than an ordinary regional loop.

prestige.explanation: The event closes a 29-season Grasshopper series and receives national coverage as an elite tune-up immediately before Unbound.

race_quality.explanation: Three aid points, wave starts, medical support, timing, photography, cash prizes, and a substantial finish party support a mature race operation.

experience.explanation: Private redwood roads, a long paved tactical middle, and the Low Gap return combine scenery and actual racing decisions.

community.explanation: The finale combines local partners, junior and team classifications, a weekend program, nonprofit support, and a devoted NorCal following.

field_depth.explanation: The 2026 race drew nationally competitive gravel and mountain-bike athletes and determined both the event podiums and overall Grasshopper elite titles.

value.explanation: Access and support are meaningful, but the completed event page does not preserve a reliable entry price for current comparison.

expenses.explanation: Northern California riders can treat Ukiah as a drive-to weekend with standard regional lodging rather than a flight-based destination.

cultural_impact.explanation: National media, elite participation, a Moriah Wilson Foundation connection, and series-finale status give it relevance beyond a local grinder.

course_description.character: A 68-percent dirt course that opens with a long climb, crosses private timber land, uses a tactical paved middle, and finishes over the classic Low Gap corridor.
course_description.signature_challenge: The top of the last major climb is not the finish: riders must still descend and manage a headwind-prone run back to Ukiah.

suffering_zones.label: Opening eight-mile climb
suffering_zones.description: Roughly 1,900 feet of gain immediately separates riders who can control early power from riders who chase the race emotionally.

suffering_zones.label: Masonite Road to Highway 128
suffering_zones.description: Private-road gravel transitions into a long paved section where small-group cooperation can save or waste the race.

suffering_zones.label: Low Gap return
suffering_zones.description: The final climb, dirt descent, and wind-exposed return demand both durability and clean tire management.

terrain.surface: 68% dirt and 32% paved on the official 2026 long course

climate.description: Cool mornings, mild-to-warm afternoons, possible residual moisture, and wind on exposed ridges.

logistics.getting_there: Base in Ukiah; the 2026 event used Todd Grove Park for packet pickup and Ukiah High School for staged starts.
logistics.accommodation: Hotels, motels, and limited event camping are available in Ukiah.
logistics.access_warning: Most private-property miles are open only to registered riders during designated event windows.

history.overview: Ukiah Mendo Gravel Epic is the season finale of the Grasshopper Adventure Series.
notable_moments: Samara Sheppard and Cole Davis won the 2026 elite races.
Jen Tavé and Cassius Anderson secured the 2026 overall Grasshopper titles at the finish.

final_verdict.one_liner: A genuine series finale: long enough to matter, steep enough to expose you, and tactical after the gravel appears to be over.
final_verdict.who_is_it_for: Gravel racers who can climb for hours, work in a group on pavement, manage puncture risk, and still descend aggressively late in the day.
final_verdict.is_it_worth_it: Yes. The organizer has confirmed the May 23, 2027 edition, and the private-road access, 8,420 feet of climbing, and field quality make it a Tier 2 target worth dedicated preparation.
pro_tips: Build durability with tempo or threshold work after three hours of endurance riding.
Practice cooperative pacing because miles 33-50 can reward a functional group.
Use modest tread and side knobs in the organizer's recommended 40-42 mm range unless final conditions say otherwise.
Keep fueling through the paved middle; the last climb and headwind still collect the bill.
